label: second input token in {o,e,n,l,g,w} (early-sequence reset unit)
explanation: Fires almost only at the start of the original phase. About 79% of activations (77% of mass) are at t=1, the second input, and there are none at t=0. Which second tokens drive it: o, e, n, l, then g, w (lift 4-7x). It also depends on the first token (prev_tok l, 3, q, x, v, c, g, f raise the rate), so it behaves like a conjunction of a first-token set and a second-token set. Adding the first-token condition gets precision to about 0.9 but halves recall. A smaller part fires at t=2-4 on first occurrences of the same tokens. About 10% of mass is on <DEL>, mostly for L=3, and this includes the strongest activations (top examples are <DEL> after 3-token sequences starting with m/v/h). It is almost silent in the copy phase and after t=5, and silent on repeated tokens and on digits as the current input. At t=1 only about 44% of the {o,e,n,l,g,w} inputs fire, so precision is limited.
